specification.name: dupr-event-api-server-data-model
specification.purpose: Shared persistence conventions and platform-owned records for a modular DUPR event API server

server.ownership: Platform records are owned by the API server; domain records are owned by their registered module.

storage.newOptionalFieldPolicy: Add a field to the owning document schema version and validator; do not add a relational column for a domain field.

documentEvolution.readerCompatibility: Readers accept the current version and explicitly supported older versions.
documentEvolution.upgradeBehavior: Use an explicit, idempotent upgrade when a default cannot preserve meaning.
documentEvolution.unknownFields: Preserve unknown fields only when they cannot affect identity, security, lifecycle, or capacity.

documentId.description: Stable identifier generated by the API server.

documentType.description: The owning module or platform record type.

commonConventions.timestamps: RFC3339 UTC strings on the API and in JSON documents.
commonConventions.nullable: Use null for a known field that is intentionally empty; omit only optional fields introduced by a later document version.
commonConventions.references: Resolve stable IDs through the owning module service; never use cross-module domain foreign keys.
commonConventions.optimisticConcurrency: Mutation requests may include an expected updatedAt or document version; stale writes fail with a typed conflict.
commonConventions.privacy: Do not store credentials, clear-text verification codes, full payment data, or unnecessary PII in platform records.

platformDocuments.purpose: At-least-once delivery of email or other platform-approved asynchronous work.
integrity: The idempotency key is unique for the owning operation.
Clear-text verification codes and credentials are never stored in payload.

platformDocuments.purpose: Redacted audit trail for platform and module mutations.
integrity: Audit details never contain credentials, verification codes, or unnecessary private data.

boundaryRules: Platform records are not domain records.
A module may create platform audit or outbox records only through the injected platform service.
A module owns and validates its domain document types in its own data-model contract.
No module may query another module's collections directly.
